questions.question_text: A plant has vascular tissue and produces spores, but no seeds. Which group best fits this combination?
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are seedless vascular plants; bryophytes lack true vascular tissue, while seed plants form seeds.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: In which plant group is the gametophyte typically the dominant, conspicuous generation, with the sporophyte dependent on it?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes have a dominant gametophyte; their sporophyte remains attached to and nutritionally dependent on it.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: A fern bears clusters of sporangia on the underside of its fronds. These clusters are called
questions.explanation: In many ferns, sporangia occur in clusters called sori, often on the lower surface of leaves.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: In Marchantia, which specialised structures contain gemmae that detach and grow into new plants?
questions.explanation: Marchantia reproduces vegetatively through gemmae produced in gemma cups; rain disperses them and each can develop into a new gametophyte.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: The jointed, ribbed stems of Equisetum are notable for accumulating which abrasive substance?
questions.explanation: Equisetum stems can accumulate silica, making them rough; horsetails are seedless vascular pteridophytes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Most pteridophytes produce one kind of spore. A pteridophyte producing distinct microspores and megaspores is described as
questions.explanation: Heterospory is production of two different spore types, commonly associated with separate male and female gametophytes and an evolutionary step toward seed habit.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which pair consists of heterosporous pteridophytes cited in standard plant classification?
questions.explanation: Selaginella and Salvinia are well-known heterosporous pteridophytes producing microspores and megaspores.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: A plant has ovules not enclosed within an ovary wall, so the mature seeds remain exposed. It belongs to
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm ovules are not enclosed by an ovary; their seeds are therefore described as naked.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: The integuments surrounding a flowering-plant ovule generally develop into which structure after fertilisation?
questions.explanation: Ovule integuments generally form the seed coat; the ovary develops into the fruit and the zygote into the embryo.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: In flowering plants, double fertilisation refers to
questions.option_a: syngamy and triple fusion in the same embryo sac
questions.option_b: two pollen grains fertilising two separate ovules
questions.option_d: fusion of two eggs with one sperm
questions.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy); the other fuses with the polar nuclei/secondary nucleus to form endosperm (triple fusion).
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which gymnosperm has coralloid roots containing nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria?
questions.explanation: Cycas bears specialised coralloid roots associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria; Pinus commonly has mycorrhizal roots.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Needle-like leaves, a thick cuticle and sunken stomata help many conifers primarily to
questions.option_a: reduce water loss in challenging environments
questions.explanation: These leaf adaptations reduce transpiration and help conifers withstand cold or dry conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which algal group is often associated with a silica-rich cell wall that can accumulate as diatomaceous earth?
questions.explanation: Diatom frustules contain silica; their deposits can form diatomaceous earth.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: A marine alga appears red because its accessory pigments mask chlorophyll. Which pigment is especially associated with red algae?
questions.explanation: Phycoerythrin is a characteristic red pigment in many Rhodophyceae and helps absorb light at depth.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which pigment is chiefly responsible for the brown colour of many brown algae?
questions.explanation: Fucoxanthin is the brown accessory pigment characteristic of many brown algae (Phaeophyceae).
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly links an alga with a common body form?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga; Volvox is colonial and Chlamydomonas is unicellular.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: A unicellular motile green alga with flagella is most likely
questions.explanation: Chlamydomonas is a unicellular, flagellated green alga; Spirogyra forms filaments and Sargassum is a brown alga.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which group contains the largest and most complex algae, including kelps?
questions.explanation: Many brown algae, especially kelps, are large multicellular marine algae with differentiated body regions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: In a bryophyte, the male gametangium that produces motile sperm is called the
questions.explanation: Antheridia are male gametangia that produce sperm; archegonia contain the egg.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Mosses lack true roots. Which structures mainly anchor them to the substratum?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes such as mosses use rhizoids for anchorage; these are not true roots with vascular tissue.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: In mosses, the capsule that produces spores belongs to which generation?
questions.explanation: The moss sporophyte includes foot, seta and capsule; the capsule produces spores by meiosis.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which statement about a fern's life cycle is correct?
questions.option_a: The conspicuous fern plant is the sporophyte, while its gametophyte is a small prothallus
questions.option_b: The fern plant is a gametophyte and produces seeds
questions.option_d: The prothallus is a cone bearing naked seeds
questions.explanation: In pteridophytes the sporophyte is dominant; the gametophyte is a small, usually independent prothallus.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: In Pinus, the ovules are borne on scales of which reproductive structure?
questions.explanation: Pinus bears ovules on the scales of female cones; pollen is produced in male cones.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: A conifer has a taproot and fungal partners around its roots that assist mineral uptake. The association is called
questions.explanation: Pinus commonly forms mycorrhizal associations between roots and fungi, aiding nutrient acquisition.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which combination is characteristic of an angiosperm rather than a gymnosperm?
questions.option_a: Flowers and seeds enclosed within fruits
questions.option_b: Naked ovules borne on cone scales
questions.option_c: Spores only and no vascular tissue
questions.option_d: A dominant gametophyte with dependent sporophyte
questions.explanation: Angiosperms are flowering plants whose ovules are enclosed in ovaries and whose seeds are enclosed in fruits.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which statement about monocot and dicot embryos is generally used in introductory classification?
questions.option_a: Monocots typically have one cotyledon and dicots typically have two
questions.option_b: Monocots have two cotyledons and dicots have none
questions.option_d: Cotyledon number distinguishes algae from fungi
questions.explanation: The number of cotyledons in the embryo is a traditional distinguishing feature: one in monocots and usually two in dicots.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which plant is a gymnosperm with an unbranched stem and large pinnate leaves?
questions.explanation: Cycas is a palm-like gymnosperm, commonly with an unbranched stem and a crown of pinnate leaves.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: Which traditional group includes simple plant-like organisms whose body is not differentiated into true roots, stems and leaves?
questions.explanation: In traditional school classification, thallophytes have a relatively undifferentiated thallus; modern classification treats many included organisms in separate kingdoms or clades.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In the moss life cycle, diploid spore mother cells in the capsule produce haploid spores by which process?
questions.explanation: Meiosis in the diploid sporophyte capsule produces haploid spores, which germinate into the gametophyte generation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class XI Biology, Plant Kingdom, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php?lebo1=13-13

questions.question_text: In most angiosperms, the pollen tube enters the ovule through the opening in its integuments called the
questions.explanation: The micropyle is the small opening in the ovule integuments through which the pollen tube commonly enters.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
